title: A PAPUA NEW GUINEA SEPIK RIVER...
reason: Hand-carved painted cowrie-eyed Sepik-style mask; age and field use unproven, but decent examples have steady collector demand.
findings: Oval board-type mask with a face carved in relief and painted in ochre, lime-white, black and yellow with dotted white outlines, two cowrie-shell eyes set in orange rings, cross-patterned discs above the eyes and a dark projecting tab at the top. The reverse is hollowed with adze or gouge marks, a dark worn patina and a string loop, which supports hand carving. No collector's label, field tag, signature or inventory number apart from the modern auction tag. Sepik River origin is plausible by style but cannot be verified or dated from the photos; many such masks were made for the trade from the 1960s on, and the paint looks fairly fresh. Size claim (H-44 cm, W-24 cm) is consistent with the proportions.
condition: Paint mostly intact with wear to the white on the face and rim edges, small knocks to the edges. No major cracks or insect holes seen.
rescore_note: Hand-carved Sepik-style board mask with cowrie eyes and decent carving, but fairly fresh paint and no field tag or provenance point to a trade piece from the 1960s on rather than an old ritual mask: middle of the $80-200 band with upside if older. Judged from photos and general market knowledge, no live comps (search limit reached).
